question.:question/problem: Which of the following diagrams gives the slope field at the points indicated for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=2-(3)xy?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We have to sketch the slope field at the points $(3,1)$,$(-1,3)$,$(0,-1)$.

To sketch the slope field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the right-hand side of the differential equation.

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(3,1)}=2-3(3)(1)=-7, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-1,3)}=2-3(-1)(3)=11, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(0,-1)}=2-3(0)(-1)=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting up our points and drawing our line segments, we get the following diagram.

![](images/eb/ebda967de728e651fa121d8f5422678825dc7ef3b24c4d1fdf61ed643d028d50.png)
